datasets: NIBRS Group A Crime Data (CSV excerpt, 1-7 June 2025, all rows with neighborhood)
311 Customer Service Requests 2025 (CSV excerpt, every 11th request, same week)
concurrency_primitives: two dataset goroutines + sync.WaitGroup (main.go:162-176); per dataset: reader goroutine -> bounded batches channel (-queue) -> N worker goroutines each owning a private Aggregator, WaitGroup then Merge, reader error via buffered errc (ingest.go:194-245); five Question goroutines over read-only Joined with per-goroutine recover (main.go:196-213); no locks (confinement)
design_patterns: Pipeline (runPipeline), Factory (crimeSpec/requestSpec/newCrimeAgg/newRequestAgg), Strategy (Aggregator, Question, Renderer interfaces each with 2+ implementations), Builder (ReportBuilder)
questions: Mayor's Office: Which neighborhoods rank highest on BOTH crime and 311 service demand, and how closely do the two track each other city-wide?
Department of Public Works: Which 311 request types are over-represented in the highest-crime neighborhoods compared with the rest of the city?
Police Department and Transportation (staffing): How do the hour-of-day profiles of crime and 311 requests compare, and where do they diverge?
Mayor's Office (service equity): Is the time to close a 311 request longer in the highest-crime neighborhoods than in the lowest-crime ones?
City Planning: Do neighborhoods with more physical-disorder 311 requests also have more violent crime?
overview: Single-package Go CLI in ten single-responsibility files: streaming CSV reader with column projection and two-allocation batches feeding a bounded worker pool per dataset, per-worker aggregators merged after wg.Wait, a quartile-labelled neighborhood join, five Question strategies run concurrently, and a ReportBuilder rendered by Text and Markdown renderers. Careful statistics (tied-rank Spearman, NaN handling), 14 tests, race-clean, MemStats reporting; README is detailed and candid (Windows-only testing, Claude assistance).
stakeholder_value: Each question stratifies one dataset by the other (crime quartiles vs 311 type lift and closure time; disorder quartiles vs violent crime; joint ranks; hourly profiles) and ends with plain-language key findings, so the Mayor's Office, DPW, Police/DOT and Planning would each get something actionable. The bundled data is a single week with a 1/11 sample of 311, so the specific numbers are illustrative; the program is ready for the full downloads but they are not included.
